title: BuildSpec — the logical indexed corpus
description: Everything that can change RESULTS, and nothing that cannot. The SHA-256 of this document canonicalized under artifact@1 is the logical index_version_id (prefixed 'idx2-'). It deliberately excludes the search engine, its revision, the envelope format, graph and quantization parameters, thread counts, the build timestamp, and query-only fusion knobs -- so rebuilding the same corpus on a newer engine produces a new ARTIFACT and not a new logical version, and a session's pin survives an engine upgrade.

spec_version.description: Schema version of this document. Not the contract VERSION and not the artifact envelope format.

scope.description: The logical scope. Tenant is supplied SEPARATELY and is never a field here: an identical corpus in two tenants is legitimately the same logical build, and tenant isolation is enforced by the catalog key and the runtime cache key, never by salting a content hash.

sources.description: Ordered, and the order is part of the identity: it is the stable source_id ordering the builder streams in, so two builds of the same set cannot disagree by permutation.

snapshot.description: The immutable point in the ledger this corpus reflects.

chunker.description: Name, version and EVERY effective parameter. 'Effective' means resolved: a default that was not written down still changes the chunks, so it is recorded here rather than left implicit.

extractor.description: Per-source extraction outcome and the hash of the text that came out. Without the per-source record, two builds whose extraction silently differed would share a logical id.

embedder.description: Null is valid and means a lexical-only corpus. An adapter must not fabricate a vector leg for one, and PreparedSearchQuery.embedding is Option for the same reason.

lexical_analysis.description: The Munarium lexical-analysis contract: everything that changes which terms exist. This is in the LOGICAL identity by the section 5.1 V1 decision, so a tokenizer change produces a new logical version that must be activated like any corpus change. The corpus-only alternative is recorded in decisions.md with its trigger.

stop_terms_ref.description: A reference plus the hash of the resolved list. A reference alone would let the list change under a fixed logical id.

positions.description: Must be true for any corpus the current shaping serves: phrase and substring demotions read positions.

reconstructed.description: True for specs reassembled from an existing PostgreSQL 'idx-' version during a mirror build. Such a spec's hash is NOT the source of the version id -- the mirror reuses the existing id -- and it must never be used as replay input, because it is a best reconstruction of inputs nobody recorded, not a record of them.
